title: Zero-Trust Connector Runway and Prioritization Playbook for Private Deploy Intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a prioritized, repeatable intake and triage playbook for private/VPC/on-prem customer requests that require zero-trust or proxy-mediated connectivity. Focus is on reducing time-to-approval for low-risk connectors, codifying staged fallback patterns for upgrades and air-gapped constraints, and creating templated comms and runbooks for SRE/Field Eng handoff. This ticket scopes the policy, scoring rubric, staging connector designs (ephemeral bastion, reverse-proxy connector, pull-based agent), and required guardrails for approvals and rollback. Goal: cut average intake-to-onboarding time for network-constrained customers from 8 weeks to 3 weeks for standard cases while preserving security posture for sensitive workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Published intake rubric that scores requests on connectivity, data sensitivity, upgrade flexibility, and legal constraints
Documentation templates for preflight probe, staged connector deployment, and rollback checklist available in Confluence
Three recommended connector archetypes defined (pull-agent, reverse-proxy bridge, ephemeral bastion) with decision matrix
A prioritized queueing policy for field requests that maps to engineering SLAs and resource buckets
Communication templates (customer ask, approval, staging plan, rollback) and a standard SLO for onboarding visibility created
Pilot with 2 enterprise customers using the new runway and documented outcomes
comments: 2026-03-01 — Created by Aisha: Initial scope drafted after 1:1s with Field Eng and two customer escalation calls where network constraints blocked upgrades. Proposed focusing on zero-trust connector patterns and a triage rubric.
2026-03-03 — Marcus: Added requirement to include KMS/HSM integration checklist for private installs; flagged this may require security team review. Linking to security review ticket once drafted.
2026-03-04 — Design sync (notes): agreed to prototype a pull-based agent first because it minimizes inbound network changes for customers. UX will need a short consent flow in Console.

2026-03-05 — Engineering feedback (Sofia Ramos): prefer reverse-proxy bridge for air-gapped customers who cannot run outbound agents. Trade-off: longer dev time and more extensive testing for TLS termination edge cases.

2026-03-07 — PM review: finalized scoring dimensions: connectivity effort (0-5), upgrade window risk (0-3), data sensitivity (0-4), regulatory constraint (0-3), business impact (0-5). Total score maps to FastTrack / Standard / Escalation lanes.

2026-03-08 — Action item: Marcus to draft preflight probe checklist + Terraform probe module; Aisha to create customer comms templates; Sofia to sketch connector deployment diagrams for both agent and reverse-proxy.
2026-03-09 — Linked artifacts: initial design doc and probe spec uploaded. Need legal signoff on reverse-proxy operator agreement for customers who require managed proxy.

2026-03-10 — Stakeholder review: Security (Eve Zhang) asked for explicit threat model and list of telemetry we collect during onboarding. Added security_review_required flag and assigned security follow-up.
Next steps: schedule pilot window with two customers (one VPC with outbound-agent allowed, one air-gapped that requires reverse-proxy). Capture timings and rollback incidents during pilot.
notes: Risk: reverse-proxy increases scope for legal and support because it may require cert management and operator agreements.
Mitigation: create two contract templates (managed-proxy consent and customer-run agent) and require legal review for managed-proxy lane.
Operationalization: Console should show connector status, last-probe timestamp, and quick rollback button that triggers staged shutdown and logs export for forensic analysis.
Metrics: track intake->approved time, approved->pilot-deployed time, pilot->production time, and number of rollback events per onboarding.
Communication play: a one-page intake form for Field Eng with mandatory probe outputs to reduce back-and-forth with customers.
